qs.e: Nagaland became the 16th state in 1963; Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura followed in 1972.

qs.q: Arrange these in the order in which they became states: Mizoram, Himachal Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim.
Which of these became a state in 1987?
qs.e: Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa became states in 1987; Meghalaya and Tripura in 1972 and Nagaland in 1963.

qs.q: Which state formed in November 2000 was carved out of Bihar?
qs.e: Chhattisgarh came from Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand from Uttar Pradesh; Telangana came in 2014.

qs.q: Telangana became India's 29th state in:
qs.e: It was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014.

qs.q: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
qs.e: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

qs.q: The Chief Election Commissioner who conducted India's first general election (1951–52) was:
qs.e: Sukumar Sen was the first CEC; the election ran from October 1951 to February 1952.

qs.q: The French settlements of Pondicherry were transferred to India de facto in:
qs.e: The de facto transfer was in 1954; the de jure transfer came in 1962.

qs.q: Which two Union Territories were merged into one in January 2020?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu
qs.e: They became one Union Territory on 26 January 2020. Ladakh and J and K were separated, not merged, in 2019.

qs.q: The state of Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into two Union Territories with effect from:
qs.e: The Act was passed in August 2019; the Union Territories of J and K and Ladakh came into being on 31 October 2019, Patel's birthday.

qs.q: Which classical dance form belongs to Tamil Nadu?
qs.e: Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance, from Tamil Nadu's Devadasi tradition.

qs.q: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance of:
qs.e: Kerala has two classical dances — Kathakali (male) and Mohiniyattam (female, solo).

qs.q: Which classical dance is associated with Andhra Pradesh?
qs.e: Kuchipudi takes its name from a village in Andhra Pradesh; Tarangam is danced on the rim of a brass plate.

qs.q: Sattriya was recognised as a classical dance form in:
qs.e: Sattriya of Assam, begun by Shankaradeva, was recognised in 2000, making the count eight.

qs.q: Which classical dance shows a strong Mughal court influence?
qs.e: Kathak developed in the Mughal courts; its gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

qs.q: The 'Tribhanga' posture is characteristic of:
qs.e: Tribhanga, a three-bend stance, is the signature of Odissi.

qs.q: Ras Leela is central to which classical dance?
qs.e: Manipuri's Ras Leela is gentle and flowing, without sharp foot-strikes.

qs.q: The Natyashastra, the oldest treatise on dance and drama, was written by:
qs.e: It is often called the fifth Veda; Nandikeshvara wrote the Abhinaya Darpana.

qs.q: Birju Maharaj was a celebrated exponent of:
qs.e: He belonged to the Lucknow gharana of Kathak.

qs.q: Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which dance form?
qs.e: He was the foremost Odissi guru of the 20th century.

qs.q: Rukmini Devi Arundale is associated with:
qs.e: She founded Kalakshetra and revived Bharatanatyam.

qs.q: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi belonged to which gharana?
qs.e: The Kirana gharana also produced Abdul Karim Khan and Gangubai Hangal.

qs.q: Ustad Bismillah Khan was a master of the:
qs.e: He was awarded the Bharat Ratna for his shehnai.

qs.q: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma popularised which instrument in classical music?
qs.e: He brought the Kashmiri santoor into Hindustani classical music.

qs.q: Amjad Ali Khan is famous for playing the:
qs.e: Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan are the best-known sarod players.

qs.q: Who is called the father of Carnatic music?
qs.e: Purandara Dasa laid its foundations; the later trinity was Tyagaraja, Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri.

qs.q: The Carnatic music trinity consists of:
o: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri
Dikshitar, Shyama Shastri and Purandara Dasa
qs.e: These three near-contemporaries defined the Carnatic kriti.

qs.q: Khayal, Thumri and Dhrupad are forms of:
qs.e: The Carnatic forms are kriti, varnam and ragam-tanam-pallavi.

qs.q: The first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna was:
qs.e: The Carnatic vocalist M. S. Subbulakshmi received it in 1998.

qs.q: How many rasas are described in Indian aesthetics?
qs.e: The Navarasa are Shringara, Hasya, Karuna, Raudra, Veera, Bhayanaka, Vibhatsa, Adbhuta and Shanta.

qs.q: The Nagara style of temple architecture is characterised by a:
qs.e: Nagara temples of the north have a curved shikhara topped by an amalaka and kalasha, and no gopuram.

qs.q: The gopuram, a tall gateway tower, is a feature of which temple style?
qs.e: Gopurams belong to the southern Dravida style.

qs.q: The Vesara style of temple architecture developed in:
qs.e: Vesara mixes Nagara and Dravida features; Pattadakal, Halebid and Belur are examples.

qs.q: The Ajanta caves contain:
qs.e: Ajanta is entirely Buddhist and famous for its paintings; Ellora has all three faiths.

qs.q: Which cave complex contains Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves?
qs.e: Ellora's 34 caves cover all three religions and include the rock-cut Kailasa temple.

qs.q: The Trimurti sculpture of Shiva is found at:
qs.e: The Maheshmurti or Trimurti is the most famous sculpture in the Elephanta caves.

qs.q: The oldest rock-cut caves in India, of the Mauryan period, are at:
qs.e: The Barabar caves, including Lomas Rishi, date from Ashoka's time.

qs.q: The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves in Odisha are:
qs.e: They are Jain caves and contain Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription.

qs.q: The hemispherical dome of a stupa is called the:
qs.e: Medhi is the base, anda the dome, harmika the square railing and yashti the mast.

qs.q: The first garden tomb built in India was:
qs.e: Humayun's tomb set the charbagh model that the Taj Mahal later perfected.

qs.q: The decorative technique of inlaying coloured stones, used in the Taj Mahal, is called:
qs.e: Pietra dura first appeared fully in Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb.

qs.q: The Alai Darwaza at the Qutub complex was built by:
qs.e: Alauddin Khalji built it in 1311 as a gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

qs.q: New Delhi was designed by:
qs.e: Lutyens and Baker designed the new capital, inaugurated in 1931.

qs.q: The Meenakshi temple at Madurai is an example of which style?
qs.e: Its towering gopurams make it a classic Dravida temple.

qs.q: The Sanchi stupa was originally built by:
qs.e: Ashoka built the core stupa; the Sungas and Satavahanas added railings and gateways.

qs.q: The largest chaitya hall in India is at:
qs.e: The Karla chaitya in Maharashtra is the biggest rock-cut chaitya hall.

qs.q: Madhubani painting belongs to:
qs.e: Madhubani or Mithila painting is done by women of the Mithila region of Bihar.

qs.q: Warli painting is a folk art of:
qs.e: Warli uses white geometric figures on a mud-red background.

qs.q: Pattachitra is a traditional painting style of:
qs.e: Pattachitra means painting on cloth, usually on Jagannath themes.

qs.q: Kalamkari painting is associated with:
qs.e: Its two schools are Srikalahasti (pen work) and Machilipatnam (block printing).

qs.q: Phad painting belongs to:
qs.e: Phad scrolls narrate the stories of the folk deities Pabuji and Devnarayan.

qs.q: Gond painting is a tribal art form of:
qs.e: Jangarh Singh Shyam brought Gond art, with its dots and dashes, to wide notice.

qs.q: Mughal painting attained its highest point under:
qs.e: Ustad Mansur's studies of birds and animals belong to Jahangir's reign.

qs.q: The Kangra school of painting belongs to which group?
qs.e: Basohli and Kangra are the two great Pahari schools.

qs.q: 'Bani-Thani' is a famous painting of which school?
qs.e: The Kishangarh school of Rajasthan produced the celebrated Bani-Thani portrait.

qs.q: The painting 'Bharat Mata' was created by:
qs.e: Abanindranath Tagore led the Bengal School; Nandalal Bose illustrated the Constitution.

qs.q: Tamasha is a folk theatre form of:
qs.e: Nautanki belongs to UP, Jatra to Bengal, Bhavai to Gujarat and Tamasha to Maharashtra.

qs.q: Yakshagana is a folk theatre form of:
qs.e: It is folk theatre, not a classical dance.

qs.q: Bhaona, or Ankia Nat, is a traditional theatre of:
qs.e: Shankaradeva created it as part of the Assamese Vaishnava tradition.

qs.q: Kathputli, the string puppet tradition, belongs to:
qs.e: Tholu Bommalata (AP) and Togalu Gombeyatta (Karnataka) are shadow puppet forms.

qs.q: Pavakoothu, a glove puppet form, belongs to:
qs.e: Putul Nautch of Bengal uses rod puppets and Ravanachhaya of Odisha shadow puppets.

qs.q: Chikankari embroidery is associated with:
qs.e: Zardozi is also associated with Lucknow and Bhopal.

qs.q: Bidriware, a metal inlay craft, comes from:
qs.e: It is named after Bidar in Karnataka.

qs.q: Patola silk sarees are woven at:
qs.e: Patola is the double-ikat weave of Patan.

qs.q: Muga silk is a speciality of:
qs.e: Muga, the golden silk, has a GI tag from Assam.

qs.q: Phulkari embroidery belongs to:
qs.e: Phulkari means 'flower work' and is done on shawls and odhnis.

qs.q: Channapatna, famous for wooden toys, is in:
qs.e: Channapatna toys, with their lacquer finish, hold a GI tag.

qs.q: Kathakali is traditionally performed by:
qs.e: Kathakali is an all-male dance-drama of Kerala with elaborate chutti make-up; Mohiniyattam is the women's solo form.

qs.q: Which is the oldest gharana of Khayal singing?
qs.e: The Gwalior gharana of Haddu and Hassu Khan is the oldest Khayal gharana.

qs.q: How many melakartas or parent scales are recognised in Carnatic music?
qs.e: Carnatic theory arranges ragas under 72 melakartas, while Hindustani music works with main ragas and their raginis.

qs.q: Zakir Hussain is a celebrated exponent of the:
qs.e: Zakir Hussain, son of Alla Rakha, is a tabla maestro; Ram Narayan is the great sarangi player.

qs.q: In Indian dance theory, 'Nritta' means:
qs.e: Nritta is pure rhythm, Nritya is expressive dance and Natya is dance-drama; Tandava is the vigorous mode.

qs.q: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, the finest Nagara temple of its group, is at:
qs.e: It stands at Khajuraho, built by the Chandelas. Konark has the Sun temple and Bhubaneswar the Lingaraja.

qs.q: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram belongs to which style?
qs.e: It is a Pallava temple in the southern Dravida style; the rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora is a different monument.

qs.q: Which caves in Madhya Pradesh have Buddhist paintings very similar to those at Ajanta?
qs.e: The Bagh caves carry Buddhist murals of the Ajanta type. Barabar in Bihar holds the oldest rock-cut caves.

qs.q: The Jain paintings at Sittanavasal are in:
qs.e: Sittanavasal in Tamil Nadu has Jain murals; Udayagiri and Khandagiri in Odisha are Jain caves without such paintings.

qs.q: The umbrella-shaped element crowning a stupa is called the:
qs.e: Above the anda sit the harmika, the yashti and the chhatra; the torana is the gateway and the medhi the base.

qs.q: The Victoria Memorial and the Writers' Building are landmarks of:
qs.e: Both are in Kolkata. The Gateway of India and CST are in Mumbai, and Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

qs.q: Pithora painting is a ritual wall art of which communities?
o: The Rathwa and Bhil of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
qs.e: Pithora paintings of ritual horses are made by Rathwa and Bhil households; Warli art is white geometric figures.

qs.q: Cheriyal scroll painting belongs to:
qs.e: Cheriyal scrolls, with their bright red backgrounds, come from Telangana; Kalamkari belongs to Andhra Pradesh.

qs.q: Dhokra, a traditional metal-casting craft, is associated with:
qs.e: Dhokra uses the lost-wax method. Bidriware is the metal inlay craft of Bidar in Karnataka.

qs.q: Therukoothu is a folk theatre form of:
qs.e: Therukoothu is Tamil street theatre; Yakshagana belongs to Karnataka and Burrakatha to Andhra Pradesh.

qs.q: Raja Ravi Varma, famous for his oil paintings on Indian themes, belonged to:
qs.e: Ravi Varma was from Kerala. The Bengal School was led by Abanindranath Tagore.

qs.q: 'Swapnavasavadatta' is a Sanskrit play by:
qs.e: Bhasa, the oldest known Sanskrit playwright, wrote Swapnavasavadatta. Shudraka wrote Mrichchhakatika, a frequent swap.

qs.q: The Sanskrit play 'Mrichchhakatika' (The Little Clay Cart) was written by:
qs.e: Shudraka's play tells of Charudatta and Vasantasena. Do not confuse it with Bhasa's Swapnavasavadatta.

qs.q: 'Kiratarjuniya', in which Arjuna fights Shiva disguised as a hunter, was composed by:
qs.e: Bharavi wrote Kiratarjuniya; Magha wrote the other Mahabharata epic, Shishupalavadha.

qs.q: 'Shishupalavadha' is the work of:
qs.e: Magha's epic tells of Krishna killing Shishupala. Bharavi's Kiratarjuniya is the poem it is usually swapped with.

qs.q: 'Dashakumaracharita', the prose tales of ten princes, was written by:
qs.e: Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita and the poetics text Kavyadarsha.

qs.q: Which play about the later life of Rama was written by Bhavabhuti?
qs.e: Bhavabhuti, at Yashovarman's court in Kannauj, wrote Uttararamacharita. Raghuvamsha is Kalidasa's poem.

qs.q: Jayadeva, the author of the Gita Govinda, was a poet at the court of:
qs.e: Jayadeva lived in 12th-century Bengal under the Sena king Lakshmana Sena.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five great Sanskrit epics (Mahakavyas)?
qs.e: The five Mahakavyas are Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Kiratarjuniya, Shishupalavadha and Naishadhiyacharita. Mrichchhakatika is a play.

qs.q: Which pair of play and author is correctly matched?
qs.e: Harsha wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda. Malatimadhava is Bhavabhuti's, Meghaduta Kalidasa's and Dashakumaracharita Dandin's.

qs.q: 'Saare Jahan Se Achha' was written by:
qs.e: Iqbal wrote it in 1904 as Tarana-e-Hind. Ghalib is the usual wrong answer.

qs.q: 'Dastanbuy', an eyewitness diary of Delhi during the revolt of 1857, was written by:
qs.e: Ghalib kept this Persian diary of 1857; Sir Syed wrote a separate essay on the causes of the revolt.

qs.q: Amir Khusrau's 'Khazain-ul-Futuh' describes the conquests of:
qs.e: Khazain-ul-Futuh records Alauddin Khalji's campaigns, including those in the south.

qs.q: 'Jana Gana Mana' was first sung in 1911 at the Congress session held at:
qs.e: It was first sung at the Calcutta session on 27 December 1911 and adopted as the anthem on 24 January 1950.

qs.q: Besides India's national anthem, Rabindranath Tagore also wrote the national anthem of:
qs.e: Tagore wrote Amar Shonar Bangla in 1905; it became Bangladesh's national anthem.

qs.q: The Hindi novel 'Godaan' was written by:
qs.e: Premchand (Dhanpat Rai Srivastava) wrote Godaan in 1936. Jaishankar Prasad wrote Kamayani.

qs.q: The poet Subramania Bharati, author of 'Panchali Sabatham', wrote in:
qs.e: Bharati is the Tamil 'Mahakavi'; Panchali Sabatham retells the Draupadi story.

qs.q: Which ancient Indian script was written from right to left?
qs.e: Kharosthi, derived from Aramaic, ran right to left. Brahmi and the scripts that grew from it run left to right.

qs.q: The Sharada script was used mainly in:
qs.e: Sharada developed in Kashmir for Kashmiri and Sanskrit; Grantha was the southern script used for Sanskrit.

qs.q: How many languages are there in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
qs.e: There were 14 in 1950; three amendments raised the number to 22. The figure of 11 is the classical languages list.

qs.q: Which language was NOT added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003)?
qs.e: The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali. Nepali came in 1992 with Konkani and Manipuri.

qs.q: Which was the first language to be declared a classical language of India, in 2004?
qs.e: Tamil came first in 2004, followed by Sanskrit in 2005 and Telugu and Kannada in 2008.

qs.q: Arrange these classical languages in the order in which they were recognised.
qs.e: Tamil 2004, Sanskrit 2005, Malayalam 2013, Odia 2014. Sanskrit did not come first.

qs.q: The first Jnanpith Award (1965) went to:
qs.e: G. Sankara Kurup won it for his Malayalam poems Odakkuzhal. Pant was the first Hindi winner, in 1968.

qs.q: The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was set up in:
qs.e: It was set up on 12 March 1954. The Jnanpith was first given in 1965.

qs.q: Which group were India's first sites on the UNESCO World Heritage List, in 1983?
o: Ajanta, Ellora, Agra Fort and Taj Mahal
Taj Mahal, Qutb Minar, Red Fort and Humayun's Tomb
qs.e: Two caves of Maharashtra and two Agra monuments came first, in 1983. The natural sites came in 1985 and 1987.

qs.q: India's only 'mixed' (cultural and natural) World Heritage Site is:
o: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers
qs.e: Khangchendzonga in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 as a mixed site. The other three are natural sites.

qs.q: Keoladeo National Park, a natural World Heritage Site, is in:
qs.e: Keoladeo, the old Bharatpur bird sanctuary, is in Rajasthan, not Gujarat.

qs.q: The Sundarbans National Park, a World Heritage Site, is known for:
o: The largest mangrove forest and the Royal Bengal tiger
qs.e: The Sundarbans in West Bengal is a mangrove delta. Rhinos mean Kaziranga and cranes mean Keoladeo.

qs.q: Rani ki Vav, the stepwell inscribed in 2014, is in which state?
qs.e: Rani ki Vav at Patan, Gujarat, was built in the 11th century under the Solankis. It appears on the ₹100 note.

qs.q: Which World Heritage Site appears on the back of the ₹100 note issued in 2018?
qs.e: Rani ki Vav is on ₹100. Hampi's chariot is on ₹50, Konark's wheel on ₹10 and Ellora on ₹20.

qs.q: The Ramappa temple, inscribed in 2021, is in:
qs.e: The Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) temple is in Telangana and is named after its sculptor. Andhra Pradesh is the usual trap.

qs.q: Which was the first Indian city to be inscribed as a World Heritage City?
qs.e: Ahmedabad was inscribed in 2017. Jaipur followed in 2019.

qs.q: In which year was Dholavira inscribed as a World Heritage Site?
qs.e: Dholavira became India's first Harappan site on the list in 2021, the same year as Ramappa.

qs.q: The Moidams, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2024, are mound burials of the:
qs.e: The Moidams of Charaideo, Assam, were inscribed at the 2024 session held in New Delhi.

qs.q: Santiniketan, inscribed in 2023, is in which state?
qs.e: Santiniketan, Tagore's university town, is in West Bengal. The Hoysala temples were inscribed in the same year.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT part of the 'Mountain Railways of India' World Heritage Site?
qs.e: The site covers Darjeeling (1999), Nilgiri (2005) and Kalka–Shimla (2008). Matheran is not part of it.

qs.q: The Capitol Complex at Chandigarh, a World Heritage Site, was designed by:
qs.e: It was inscribed in 2016 as part of Le Corbusier's architectural work across several countries. Lutyens designed New Delhi.

qs.q: Arrange these World Heritage Sites by the year they were inscribed, earliest first.
o: Taj Mahal, Sanchi, Red Fort, Rani ki Vav
Sanchi, Taj Mahal, Rani ki Vav, Red Fort
Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Sanchi, Rani ki Vav
Red Fort, Taj Mahal, Sanchi, Rani ki Vav
qs.e: Taj Mahal 1983, Sanchi 1989, Red Fort 2007, Rani ki Vav 2014.

qs.q: Which site-state pair is correctly matched?
o: Great Himalayan National Park – Himachal Pradesh
qs.e: The Great Himalayan NP is in Himachal. Manas is in Assam, Champaner-Pavagadh in Gujarat and Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh.

qs.q: Which fort in Tamil Nadu is part of the 'Maratha Military Landscapes' inscribed in 2025?
qs.e: The site has 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee in Tamil Nadu.

qs.q: Which element was added to UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list from India in 2023?
qs.e: Garba was inscribed in 2023. Durga Puja was added in 2021, Kumbh Mela in 2017 and Yoga in 2016.

qs.q: Ramman, on UNESCO's intangible heritage list, is a religious festival and ritual theatre of:
qs.e: Ramman belongs to the Garhwal Himalayas in Uttarakhand and was inscribed in 2009.

qs.q: Kalbelia folk songs and dances, on UNESCO's intangible list, belong to:
qs.e: Kalbelia of Rajasthan was inscribed in 2010 along with Mudiyettu and Chhau.

qs.q: The Thatheras of Jandiala Guru, on UNESCO's intangible list, are known for:
qs.e: This Punjab craft of beaten brass and copper vessels was inscribed in 2014.

qs.q: Mudiyettu, a ritual dance-drama on UNESCO's intangible list, comes from:
qs.e: Mudiyettu of Kerala was inscribed in 2010. Koodiyattam, also from Kerala, was inscribed in 2008.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list for India?
qs.e: Kerala's Koodiyattam and Mudiyettu are listed, and so is Chhau. Kathakali is not on the list.

qs.q: 'Durga Puja in Kolkata' was added to UNESCO's intangible heritage list in:
qs.e: Durga Puja was inscribed in 2021. Kumbh Mela came in 2017 and Garba in 2023.

qs.q: The Bastille fell on:
qs.e: The fall of the Bastille is treated as the start of the French Revolution.

qs.q: 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity' was the slogan of the:
qs.e: The French Revolution of 1789 gave the world this slogan.

qs.q: The Social Contract was written by:
qs.e: Montesquieu wrote The Spirit of the Laws, setting out the separation of powers.

qs.q: The American Declaration of Independence was adopted on:
qs.e: Thomas Jefferson drafted it; the Boston Tea Party was in 1773.

qs.q: 'No taxation without representation' was the slogan of the:
qs.e: The American colonists objected to being taxed without seats in Parliament.

qs.q: The steam engine was improved and made practical by:
qs.e: Hargreaves made the spinning jenny, Arkwright the water frame and Cartwright the power loom.

qs.q: The Bolshevik Revolution took place in:
qs.e: The February Revolution ended the Tsar; the October Revolution brought Lenin to power.

qs.q: 'Peace, Land and Bread' was the slogan of:
qs.e: It summed up the Bolshevik promise in 1917.

qs.q: The last Tsar of Russia was:
qs.e: Nicholas II abdicated in March 1917 and was later executed.

qs.q: The First World War was triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at:
qs.e: He was shot on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip.

qs.q: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on:
qs.e: It punished Germany with the war-guilt clause, reparations and loss of colonies.

qs.q: The League of Nations had its headquarters at:
qs.e: It was set up in 1920 on Woodrow Wilson's proposal, though the USA never joined.

qs.q: The Fourteen Points were put forward by:
qs.e: The US President's Fourteen Points included the idea of a League of Nations.

qs.q: The Second World War began with Germany's invasion of:
The atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on:
qs.e: Hiroshima came first (Little Boy) and Nagasaki on 9 August (Fat Man).

qs.q: The United Nations came into existence on:
qs.e: The Charter was signed on 26 June at San Francisco and came into force on 24 October — UN Day.

qs.q: The unification of Germany in 1871 was achieved under:
qs.e: Bismarck's 'blood and iron' policy unified Germany; Garibaldi, Cavour and Mazzini unified Italy.

qs.q: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed in 1949 by:
qs.e: Sun Yat-sen had ended the Manchu dynasty in 1911.

qs.q: The Meiji Restoration of 1868 took place in:
qs.e: It began Japan's rapid modernisation under imperial rule.

qs.q: D-Day, the Allied landing in Normandy, took place on:
qs.e: Pearl Harbor was attacked on 7 December 1941; Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945.

qs.q: The traveller who wrote the 'Rehla' and served as Qazi of Delhi came from:
qs.e: Ibn Battuta of Morocco came under Muhammad bin Tughlaq and wrote the Rehla (Kitab-ul-Rehla).

qs.q: Marco Polo visited which Indian kingdom?
qs.e: He visited the Pandya kingdom in the late 13th century.

qs.q: 'Kitab-ul-Hind' was written by:
qs.e: Al-Beruni came with Mahmud of Ghazni; the work is also called Tahqiq-i-Hind.

qs.q: Abdur Razzaq, the Persian envoy, visited the court of:
qs.e: Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I and Abdur Razzaq under Devaraya II.

qs.q: Domingo Paes visited the court of:
qs.e: The Portuguese traveller left a vivid description of Vijayanagara at its height.

qs.q: Who is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
qs.e: Naoroji was also the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament.

qs.q: Who gave Gandhi the title 'Father of the Nation'?
qs.e: Tagore called him Mahatma; Bose called him Father of the Nation.

qs.q: Lala Lajpat Rai was known as:
qs.e: Deshbandhu was C. R. Das, Lokmanya was Tilak and Loknayak was Jayaprakash Narayan.

qs.q: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly called:
qs.e: He was also known as Badshah Khan and led the Khudai Khidmatgars.

qs.q: Samudragupta is called the:
qs.e: V. A. Smith gave him the title for his wide conquests.

qs.q: Amir Khusrau was called:
qs.e: Hiuen Tsang was the Prince of Pilgrims and Aurangzeb the Zinda Pir.

qs.q: 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' was the slogan of:
qs.e: Shastri gave it during the 1965 war.

qs.q: The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' is associated with:
qs.e: It was coined by the poet Hasrat Mohani and made famous by Bhagat Singh.

qs.q: 'Vande Mataram' first appeared in which work?
qs.e: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee included it in Anandamath (1882).

qs.q: Who coined the slogans 'Quit India' and 'Simon Go Back'?
qs.e: The Bombay socialist Yusuf Meherally coined both.

qs.q: 'India Wins Freedom' was written by:
qs.e: It is Azad's account of the years before Partition.

qs.q: 'Gita Rahasya' was written by:
qs.e: Tilak wrote it while imprisoned at Mandalay.

qs.q: 'Why I am an Atheist' was written by:
qs.e: Bhagat Singh wrote it in jail in 1930.

qs.q: 'The Indian Struggle' was written by:
qs.e: Savarkar wrote The Indian War of Independence 1857 and Lajpat Rai Unhappy India.

qs.q: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913 for:
qs.e: He was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize for Literature.

qs.q: 'Annihilation of Caste' was written by:
qs.e: It was written in 1936 as an undelivered speech.

qs.q: Lord Ripon is called the Father of:
qs.e: Cornwallis is the father of the Indian civil services and Dalhousie is called the maker of modern India.

qs.q: The Glorious Revolution of 1688 took place in:
qs.e: The bloodless revolution of 1688 in England led to the Bill of Rights of 1689 and the supremacy of Parliament.

qs.q: The Reign of Terror during the French Revolution is associated with:
qs.e: Robespierre led the Jacobin Reign of Terror; Napoleon seized power in 1799.

qs.q: The spinning jenny was invented by:
qs.e: Hargreaves made the spinning jenny, Arkwright the water frame, Crompton the mule and Watt improved the steam engine.

qs.q: Japan formally surrendered in the Second World War on:
qs.e: Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945 and Japan on 2 September 1945, after the atom bombs of 6 and 9 August.

qs.q: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk of 1918 was signed between Germany and:
qs.e: Lenin's government signed it to take Russia out of the First World War.

qs.q: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India in the late seventh century, after Hiuen Tsang?
qs.e: I-tsing came in the late 7th century. Fa-Hien had come under Chandragupta II and Hiuen Tsang under Harsha.

qs.q: Who is known as the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'?
qs.e: Bhikaji Cama unfurled an early version of the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907. Sarojini Naidu was the Nightingale of India.

qs.q: Rabindranath Tagore was given the title 'Gurudev' by:
qs.e: Gandhi called Tagore 'Gurudev', and Tagore in turn called Gandhi 'Mahatma'.

qs.q: The slogan 'Aram Haram Hai' was given by:
qs.e: Nehru coined it, and also asked 'Who lives if India dies?'; Shastri gave 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'.

qs.q: 'Gita Govinda' was written by:
qs.e: Jayadeva's Sanskrit Gita Govinda celebrates Radha and Krishna; Jnaneshwar wrote the Marathi Jnaneshwari.

qs.q: 'Glimpses of World History' was written by:
qs.e: Nehru wrote it as letters to his daughter, and also wrote The Discovery of India.

qs.q: The Code of Hammurabi, one of the earliest written law codes, belongs to:
qs.e: Hammurabi of Babylon issued his code around 1750 BCE in Mesopotamia, between the Tigris and the Euphrates.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The wedge-shaped cuneiform script was developed in:
qs.e: The Sumerians of Mesopotamia pressed cuneiform into clay. Egypt used hieroglyphics.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Egyptian hieroglyphics were deciphered with the help of the Rosetta Stone by:
qs.e: Champollion read the hieroglyphs in 1822. Prinsep deciphered India's Brahmi script.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Which river is called 'China's Sorrow'?
qs.e: The Huang He (Yellow River), the cradle of Chinese civilisation, floods often, hence 'China's Sorrow'.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Alexander defeated Porus in 326 BCE at the Battle of the Hydaspes, fought on the banks of the:
qs.e: The Hydaspes is the Greek name for the Jhelum. The Beas is where Alexander's army refused to go further.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Alexander's army refused to march further east at the banks of the:
qs.e: At the Beas (Hyphasis) his tired soldiers refused to go on, and he turned back. He died at Babylon in 323 BCE.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Who was the tutor of Alexander the Great?
qs.e: Aristotle, Plato's pupil, taught the young Alexander in Macedon.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Arrange in order of teacher to pupil:
qs.e: Socrates taught Plato, Plato taught Aristotle, and Aristotle taught Alexander.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
qs.e: Octavian took the title Augustus in 27 BCE. Julius Caesar was a dictator but never emperor.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: 'Veni, vidi, vici' (I came, I saw, I conquered) is a saying of:
qs.e: Julius Caesar reported his quick victory with these words. He was killed in 44 BCE.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Confucius, whose sayings are collected in the Analects, was a thinker from:
qs.e: Confucius (551–479 BCE) lived in China around the same time as the Buddha and Mahavira.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The holy book of Zoroastrianism is the:
qs.e: Zoroaster's teachings are in the Avesta. The Torah is Jewish and the Analects are Confucian.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The Hijra of 622 CE, from which the Islamic calendar begins, refers to the Prophet's migration from:
qs.e: Prophet Muhammad moved from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE; he died at Medina in 632 CE.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The Magna Carta of 1215 was accepted by which English king?
qs.e: King John accepted it at Runnymede under pressure from his barons. The 1689 Bill of Rights is a different document.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The Renaissance began in the 14th century in:
qs.e: It began in Italian cities such as Florence, with patrons like the Medici family.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel was painted by:
qs.e: Michelangelo painted the Sistine ceiling and carved David. Leonardo painted the Mona Lisa.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: 'Mona Lisa' and 'The Last Supper' were painted by:
qs.e: Both are Leonardo's. Raphael painted the School of Athens.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Johannes Gutenberg, who built a movable-type printing press around 1440, came from:
qs.e: Gutenberg worked at Mainz in Germany; his printed Bible appeared around 1455.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The Protestant Reformation began in 1517 when the Ninety-five Theses were posted by:
qs.e: Luther protested against the sale of indulgences. Loyola founded the Jesuits of the Counter-Reformation.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Constantinople fell in 1453 to the:
qs.e: Mehmed II took the city, ending the Byzantine Empire; the blocked land route pushed Europeans to look for a sea route to India.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: The first voyage around the world (1519–22) was led by:
qs.e: Magellan's expedition went round the world, though he was killed in the Philippines in 1521 and Elcano finished the voyage.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Brazil was reached for Portugal in 1500 by:
qs.e: Cabral reached Brazil on his way to India, which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Arrange these voyages in chronological order.
o: Dias rounds the Cape, Columbus reaches America, Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, Magellan sets out
Columbus reaches America, Dias rounds the Cape, Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, Magellan sets out
Dias rounds the Cape, Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, Columbus reaches America, Magellan sets out
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, Dias rounds the Cape, Columbus reaches America, Magellan sets out
qs.e: Dias 1488, Columbus 1492, Vasco da Gama 1498, Magellan 1519.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Christopher Columbus made his voyage of 1492 on behalf of:
qs.e: Columbus, from Genoa in Italy, sailed for Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain. Vasco da Gama sailed for Portugal.
qs.tag: The ancient world to the Age of Discovery

qs.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Computer'?
qs.e: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine, the plan of the modern computer. Turing is linked to theoretical computer science and AI.

qs.q: Who is regarded as the world's first computer programmer?
qs.e: Ada Lovelace wrote an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843.

qs.q: What is the full form of ENIAC?
qs.e: ENIAC (1946), built by Eckert and Mauchly, was the first general-purpose electronic computer and used vacuum tubes.

qs.q: What is the full form of UNIVAC?
qs.e: UNIVAC I (1951) was the first commercially produced computer in the USA — not the first electronic computer, which was ENIAC.

qs.q: Which technology was used in first-generation computers?
qs.e: First generation (about 1940–56) used vacuum tubes: huge, hot and power-hungry. Transistors came in the second generation.

qs.q: Microprocessors (VLSI) are the main technology of which generation of computers?
qs.e: IC = third generation; VLSI microprocessor = fourth; AI = fifth. Exams often swap third and fourth.

qs.q: Which pair of generation and technology is correctly matched?
qs.e: Order: vacuum tube, transistor, IC, microprocessor, artificial intelligence.

qs.q: Fifth-generation computers are mainly based on:
qs.e: Fifth generation aims at AI — natural language, expert systems, parallel processing.

qs.q: Who built the Pascaline, an early mechanical adding machine (1642)?
qs.e: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline. Napier gave Napier's Bones; Hollerith the punched-card tabulator.

qs.q: Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulating machine was first used for:
qs.e: Hollerith's machine processed the 1890 US census; his company later became IBM. Punched cards for weaving were Jacquard's.

qs.q: The 'stored-program' concept, in which instructions and data share the same memory, is credited to:
qs.e: Von Neumann's 1945 EDVAC report described the stored-program architecture used by almost all computers today.

qs.q: Which was the first commercially produced computer in the USA?
qs.e: UNIVAC I (1951) was sold commercially; ENIAC (1946) was a government/university machine.

qs.q: India's first supercomputer, PARAM 8000 (1991), was developed by:
qs.e: C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, led by Vijay Bhatkar, built PARAM 8000 in 1991.

qs.q: A speedometer of a car is an example of which type of computer/device?
qs.e: Analog devices measure continuous quantities such as speed, temperature or voltage.

qs.q: A computer used in a hospital ICU that measures heartbeat (analog) and displays it as numbers (digital) is a:
qs.e: Hybrid computers combine analog and digital features — ECG/ICU machines, petrol pumps.

qs.q: Which type of computer is used for weather forecasting and nuclear research?
qs.e: Supercomputers are the fastest; their speed is measured in FLOPS. Mainframes serve banks and railways.

qs.q: Arrange computers in increasing order of size and power.
qs.e: Smallest to largest: microcomputer, minicomputer, mainframe, supercomputer.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a computer?
qs.e: A computer is fast, accurate and tireless, but it has no intelligence or feelings of its own.

qs.q: The term GIGO in computing stands for:
qs.e: GIGO means wrong input data produces wrong output — the computer itself does not make errors.

qs.q: Raw, unprocessed facts given to a computer are called:
qs.e: Data is raw facts; information is data after processing.

qs.q: Large organisations such as banks and railway reservation systems, with thousands of users at once, typically use:
qs.e: Mainframes handle huge numbers of simultaneous users and transactions.

qs.q: Which device invented in 1947 at Bell Labs replaced vacuum tubes in computers?
qs.e: The transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley) made second-generation computers smaller, faster and cooler.

qs.q: Which was the first commercial microprocessor (1971)?
qs.e: The 4-bit Intel 4004 was released in 1971 and began the fourth generation.

qs.q: What is the full form of CPU?
qs.e: The CPU is the brain of the computer, made of the CU, ALU and registers.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical (comparison) operations?
qs.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit calculates and compares; the Control Unit only directs and coordinates.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which unit of the CPU directs and coordinates all operations of the computer but does not process data itself?
qs.e: The CU fetches and decodes instructions and sends control signals; the ALU does the actual calculating.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: What is the full form of BIOS?
qs.e: BIOS is firmware stored in ROM/flash that runs POST and starts booting.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: What is the full form of POST?
qs.e: POST is run by the BIOS at start-up to check RAM, keyboard and drives.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Restarting a computer that is already switched on is called:
qs.e: Warm boot = restart (or Ctrl+Alt+Del); cold boot = starting from power off.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: What is the full form of SMPS?
qs.e: SMPS converts mains AC into the low-voltage DC used inside the computer. A UPS gives battery back-up.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: What is the full form of USB?
qs.e: USB is a serial, plug-and-play, hot-swappable port; one controller can support up to 127 devices.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which port carries both high-definition video and audio in a single digital cable?
qs.e: HDMI = High-Definition Multimedia Interface. VGA carries analog video only.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: What is the full form of VGA?
qs.e: VGA is the older analog 15-pin video port for monitors and projectors.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be executed?
qs.e: The Program Counter points to the next instruction; the Instruction Register holds the current one.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Arrange the steps of the machine (instruction) cycle in the correct order.
qs.e: The CPU fetches an instruction, decodes it, executes it and stores (writes back) the result.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: The clock speed of a processor is measured in:
qs.e: Clock speed is cycles per second, in hertz; modern CPUs run at several GHz.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which bus is unidirectional, carrying memory locations from the CPU to memory?
qs.e: The address bus is one-way; the data bus is two-way; the control bus carries signals.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: The main circuit board of a computer that holds the CPU, RAM and expansion slots is the:
qs.e: The motherboard (system board/main board) connects all parts.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which small battery on the motherboard keeps the date, time and BIOS settings when the computer is off?
qs.e: The CMOS battery is a coin cell that powers the BIOS settings memory and real-time clock.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: A parallel port sends data:
o: Several bits at the same time
qs.e: Parallel (LPT) ports sent 8 bits at once, used for old printers; serial ports send one bit at a time.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which connector is used for a wired Ethernet (LAN) cable?
qs.e: RJ-45 is the 8-pin Ethernet jack; RJ-11 is the smaller telephone jack.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: The round PS/2 ports on older computers were used to connect:
qs.e: PS/2: purple for keyboard, green for mouse. USB has now replaced them.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a part of the CPU?
qs.e: The hard disk is secondary storage outside the CPU.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: BIOS is stored in which type of memory?
qs.e: BIOS is firmware in ROM/flash so it survives power-off. RAM is volatile.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Speed of a computer in terms of instructions is commonly expressed in:
qs.e: MIPS = Million Instructions Per Second. RPM is for hard disks; PPM for printers; DPI for print resolution.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which expansion card lets a computer connect to a network?
qs.e: A Network Interface Card fits in an expansion slot (or is built in) and provides the RJ-45 port.
qs.tag: Inside the computer: CPU, motherboard & ports

qs.q: Which device is used by banks to read the numbers printed at the bottom of cheques?
qs.e: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads characters printed in magnetic ink on cheques.

qs.q: What is the full form of MICR?
qs.e: MICR is used in banks for cheque processing.

qs.q: Which device is used to check objective-type answer sheets with filled bubbles?
qs.e: OMR (Optical Mark Recognition/Reader) detects darkened marks. OCR reads text characters.

qs.q: Which technology converts a scanned page of printed text into editable text?
Which of these is an impact printer?
qs.e: Impact printers strike the paper: dot matrix, daisy wheel, line printer. Laser, inkjet and thermal are non-impact.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT an impact printer?
qs.e: A laser printer uses toner and a laser-charged drum without striking the paper.

qs.q: Which printer is used for ATM slips and shop bill receipts on heat-sensitive paper?
qs.e: Thermal printers use heat on special paper.

qs.q: Which device is used to print large engineering drawings, maps and CAD designs?
qs.e: Plotters (flatbed or drum) are output devices for large-format drawings.

qs.q: Which of the following is both an input and an output device?
qs.e: A touch screen takes input by touch and shows output on the same screen.

qs.q: What is the full form of LCD?
qs.e: LCD panels use liquid crystals and need a backlight.

qs.q: What is the full form of CRT?
qs.e: CRT monitors used an electron gun; bulky and heavy.

qs.q: In OLED displays, the letter 'O' stands for:
qs.e: OLED = Organic Light Emitting Diode; each pixel gives its own light, so no backlight is needed.

qs.q: The smallest single dot of a picture on a display screen is called a:
qs.e: Pixel = Picture Element. Resolution is counted in pixels, e.g. 1920 × 1080.

qs.q: DPI, used to describe printer quality, stands for:
qs.e: DPI measures print/scan resolution; PPI (Pixels Per Inch) is for screens.

qs.q: The keyboard layout used on most computers is named after:
o: The first six letters of the top letter row
qs.e: QWERTY comes from the letters Q W E R T Y on the top letter row; designed by Christopher Latham Sholes for typewriters.

qs.q: Which of these is a toggle key on a keyboard?
qs.e: Toggle keys switch a mode on/off: Caps Lock, Num Lock, Scroll Lock. Shift works only while held.

qs.q: Who invented the computer mouse?
qs.e: Douglas Engelbart developed the mouse in the 1960s.

qs.q: A light pen is mainly used to:
o: Draw or select directly on the screen
qs.e: A light pen is a light-sensitive input device used to point and draw on screen.

qs.q: Printed output on paper is called:
qs.e: Hard copy is printed and permanent; soft copy is shown on the screen.

qs.q: Which pair of device and use is correctly matched?
o: Barcode reader — billing at a shop counter
qs.e: Barcode readers are used at POS billing; MICR is for cheques and OMR for answer sheets.

qs.q: The speed of a laser printer is usually measured in:
qs.e: Laser = PPM, dot matrix = CPS, line printer = LPM. DPI is quality, not speed.

qs.q: Which of the following is an output device?
qs.e: A projector shows the screen on a wall. Joystick, scanner and webcam are input devices.

qs.q: Which input device is used for Aadhaar-based fingerprint authentication?
qs.e: Biometric devices read fingerprints, iris or face to identify a person.

qs.q: CRT, an older type of monitor, stands for:
qs.e: CRT monitors fire electron beams from a cathode ray tube at a phosphor screen; they were replaced by flat LCD and LED panels.

qs.q: LCD stands for:
qs.e: LCD = Liquid Crystal Display. An 'LED monitor' is usually an LCD panel lit from behind by LEDs.

qs.q: Which of the following memories is volatile?
qs.e: RAM loses its contents when power is switched off; ROM, EPROM and hard disks do not.

qs.q: 1 nibble is equal to:
qs.e: A nibble is half a byte: 4 bits. A byte is 8 bits.

qs.q: What is the smallest unit of data in a computer?
qs.e: A bit (binary digit) is a single 0 or 1.

qs.q: Which of these is the largest unit of memory?
qs.e: Order: KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB. Yottabyte is the largest in the usual exam list.

qs.q: 1 KB (in binary, as used for memory) equals:
qs.e: 1 KB = 2^10 = 1024 bytes. Disk makers use the decimal 1000.

qs.q: Arrange in increasing order: GB, KB, TB, MB.
qs.e: Each unit is 1024 times the previous: KB, MB, GB, TB.

qs.q: How many bits are there in 1 KB?
What is the full form of ROM?
qs.e: ROM is non-volatile and stores firmware such as BIOS.

qs.q: Which type of ROM is erased using ultraviolet light?
qs.e: EPROM = Erasable Programmable ROM, erased by UV light. EEPROM is erased electrically.

qs.q: What is the full form of EEPROM?
o: Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
Electronically Erasable Permanent Read Only Memory
Extended Erasable Programmable Read Only Memory
Electrically Editable Programmable Random Only Memory
qs.e: EEPROM is erased and rewritten electrically; flash memory is a type of EEPROM.

qs.q: A PROM chip can be programmed by the user:
o: Any number of times with UV light
qs.e: PROM is one-time programmable. EPROM (UV) and EEPROM (electric) can be erased.

qs.q: Which is the fastest memory in a computer?
qs.e: Registers are inside the CPU and are the fastest; cache comes next.

qs.q: Which high-speed memory sits between the CPU and the main memory (RAM) to hold frequently used data?
qs.e: Cache (L1, L2, L3) is made of SRAM and reduces the time the CPU waits for RAM.

qs.q: Cache memory is usually made of:
qs.e: SRAM is fast and needs no refreshing, so it is used for cache; DRAM is used for main memory.

qs.q: Which RAM needs to be refreshed thousands of times per second because it stores bits in capacitors?
qs.e: Dynamic RAM uses capacitors that leak charge, so it must be refreshed. Static RAM uses flip-flops.

qs.q: Which of these is directly accessed by the CPU?
qs.e: The CPU reads primary memory directly; data on secondary storage must first be loaded into RAM.

qs.q: Using part of the hard disk as if it were extra RAM is called:
qs.e: Virtual memory (page file/swap) lets programs run when RAM is full, at slower speed.

qs.q: Arrange the following in decreasing order of speed: RAM, Registers, Hard disk, Cache.
qs.e: Memory hierarchy: registers, cache, RAM, secondary storage.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT volatile?
qs.e: Only ROM keeps data without power here; RAM, cache and registers are volatile.

qs.q: Software permanently stored in ROM, such as the BIOS, is called:
qs.e: Firmware is software held in non-volatile memory chips.

qs.q: Which cache level is the smallest and fastest?
qs.e: L1 is inside each core and fastest; L2 is larger; L3 is largest and shared by cores.

qs.q: How many bytes are there in 1 MB (binary)?
Which of these memories works directly with the CPU, sitting between it and RAM?
qs.e: Cache is small, very fast memory that feeds the CPU the data it needs next. The others are secondary storage, far slower and not accessed directly by the CPU.

qs.q: What is the full form of HDD?
qs.e: An HDD stores data magnetically on spinning platters.

qs.q: What is the full form of SSD?
qs.e: An SSD uses flash memory chips and has no moving parts.

qs.q: Which storage device has no moving parts?
qs.e: SSDs use NAND flash chips, so they are faster, silent and shock-resistant.

qs.q: Which storage medium allows only sequential access?
qs.e: Tape must be wound to the right place; it is used for cheap archival back-ups.

qs.q: The concentric circles on the surface of a hard disk platter are called:
qs.e: Tracks are circles; sectors are pie-shaped slices of a track.

qs.q: A pie-shaped division of a track on a disk is called a:
qs.e: A sector is the smallest storage block on a disk, traditionally 512 bytes.

qs.q: What is the typical storage capacity of a standard CD?
qs.e: CD about 700 MB, DVD 4.7 GB, Blu-ray 25 GB, 3.5-inch floppy 1.44 MB.

qs.q: What is the capacity of a single-layer DVD?
What is the full form of DVD?
qs.e: DVD = Digital Versatile Disc (also called Digital Video Disc).

qs.q: A single-layer Blu-ray disc can store about:
qs.e: Blu-ray uses a blue-violet laser with a shorter wavelength, so it packs 25 GB per layer.

qs.q: Arrange in increasing order of capacity: DVD, CD, Blu-ray, floppy disk.
The capacity of a standard 3.5-inch floppy disk is:
qs.e: The common 3.5-inch high-density floppy held 1.44 MB.

qs.q: CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray discs are read using:
qs.e: They are optical media; data is stored as pits and lands read by laser.

qs.q: A CD-R disc can be:
o: Written once and read many times
Only read, never written by the user
qs.e: CD-R is WORM (Write Once Read Many); CD-RW can be rewritten.

qs.q: Which back-up copies only the data changed since the last full back-up?
qs.e: Differential counts from the last FULL back-up; incremental counts from the last back-up of any type.

qs.q: Which back-up type is fastest to create but needs the full back-up plus every later back-up to restore?
qs.e: Incremental copies only changes since the last back-up, so each is small, but restoring needs the whole chain.

qs.q: Which of these is an example of cloud storage?
qs.e: Cloud storage keeps files on remote servers reached via the internet: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox.

qs.q: DigiLocker, used to store documents like Aadhaar and mark sheets, is a:
o: Government of India cloud storage service
qs.e: DigiLocker is the Government of India's cloud locker for official documents.

qs.q: Which file system is the default for Windows hard disks?
qs.e: NTFS = New Technology File System. ext4 is Linux; APFS is Apple's.

qs.q: The maximum size of a single file on a FAT32 drive is:
qs.e: FAT32 cannot hold a single file larger than 4 GB; NTFS or exFAT are used for bigger files.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an optical storage device?
qs.e: A pen drive uses flash memory; the others are read by laser.

qs.q: The time taken by a hard disk's read/write head to move to the correct track is called:
qs.e: Seek time is head movement; rotational latency is the wait for the sector to spin under the head.

qs.q: A storage device that combines flash memory with a built-in USB interface is a:
qs.e: A pen drive (USB flash drive) is flash memory with a USB plug: no moving parts, rewritable and portable.

qs.q: DVD stands for:
qs.e: DVD = Digital Versatile Disc (often also expanded as Digital Video Disc). A single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 GB.

qs.q: What is the base of the hexadecimal number system?
What is the base of the octal number system?
Convert (25) in decimal to binary.
qs.e: 25 = 16 + 8 + 1 = 11001. Read remainders of repeated division by 2 from bottom to top.

qs.q: What is the decimal value of binary 1011?
What is the decimal value of hexadecimal 2F?
Convert octal 156 to decimal.
Convert binary 101101 to octal.
qs.e: Group in threes from the right: 101 | 101 = 5 5, so (55) octal. Its decimal value is 45 and hex 2D.

qs.q: Convert binary 101101 to hexadecimal.
qs.e: Group in fours from the right: 0010 | 1101 = 2 D.

qs.q: Hexadecimal A5 written in binary is:
The decimal number 255 in hexadecimal is:
qs.e: 255 = 11111111 in binary = FF in hex = 377 in octal; it is the largest value in 8 bits.

qs.q: How many binary bits represent one hexadecimal digit?
qs.e: 16 = 2^4, so each hex digit equals 4 bits; each octal digit equals 3 bits.

qs.q: How many binary bits represent one octal digit?
The result of binary addition 1011 + 1101 is:
In the hexadecimal system, the symbol F represents the decimal value:
What is the full form of ASCII?
o: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for Internal Information
Automatic Standard Code for Information Interchange
American System Code for Information Interface
qs.e: ASCII is a 7-bit code with 128 characters; 'A' = 65.

qs.q: How many characters can standard 7-bit ASCII represent?
What is the full form of EBCDIC?
o: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
Extended Binary Character Data Interchange Code
Electronic Binary Coded Decimal Information Code
Extended Basic Coded Decimal Interchange Code
qs.e: EBCDIC is an 8-bit code used mainly on IBM mainframes.

qs.q: Which character encoding can represent scripts of almost all world languages, including Hindi?
qs.e: Unicode (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32) covers almost every script and emoji.

qs.q: Which logic gates are called universal gates?
qs.e: Any other gate can be built using only NAND gates or only NOR gates.

qs.q: Which gate gives output 1 only when both inputs are 1?
qs.e: AND outputs 1 only for inputs 1 and 1.

qs.q: Which gate gives output 1 only when its two inputs are different?
qs.e: XOR (exclusive OR): 0,1 and 1,0 give 1; equal inputs give 0. XNOR is the reverse.

qs.q: For a NOR gate, the output is 1 when:
qs.e: NOR = NOT of OR: output is 1 only when no input is 1.

qs.q: The ASCII code of the capital letter 'A' is:
The 1's complement of binary 1010 is:
qs.e: 1's complement flips every bit; 2's complement adds 1 to it.

qs.q: Which of the following is system software?
qs.e: The operating system controls the computer and is system software; Word, Tally and VLC do user tasks and are application software.

qs.q: A compiler translates a high-level program —
o: all at once, into machine code, before it runs
one line at a time while it runs
only from assembly language to machine code
from RAM to the hard disk
qs.e: A compiler converts the whole program in one go and lists the errors afterwards; line-by-line translation is the interpreter's way.

qs.q: Which translator converts and executes a high-level program one statement at a time?
qs.e: An interpreter translates and runs line by line and stops at the first error; a compiler translates the whole program first.

qs.q: An assembler converts —
o: source code into a web page
qs.e: The assembler works only on assembly language (mnemonics such as ADD, MOV); compilers and interpreters handle high-level languages.

qs.q: Which program places an executable program into main memory so that it can run?
qs.e: The loader (part of the OS) loads the program into RAM; the linker only joins object files into one executable.

qs.q: Which program joins several object files and library files into a single executable file?
qs.e: The linker combines object modules into one executable; the loader later places that file in memory.

qs.q: Machine language, written only in 0s and 1s, belongs to which generation of programming languages?
qs.e: 1GL = machine language, 2GL = assembly language, 3GL = high-level languages such as C and Java.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a high-level language?
qs.e: Assembly language is a low-level (second-generation) language using mnemonics; COBOL, Python and FORTRAN are high-level.

qs.q: SQL is generally classed as a language of which generation?
qs.e: SQL is a 4GL — you state what data you want, not how to get it; Prolog is the usual 5GL example.

qs.q: Which of the following operating systems is open source?
qs.e: Linux (first released by Linus Torvalds in 1991) is open source; Windows, macOS and MS-DOS are proprietary.

qs.q: The Android operating system is built on which kernel?
qs.e: Android, developed by Google, uses a modified Linux kernel; iOS is Apple's mobile OS.

qs.q: Which type of operating system is used where a response must come within a fixed time limit, such as air-traffic control or missile guidance?
qs.e: A real-time OS (RTOS) must respond within strict deadlines; batch systems run collected jobs with no user interaction.

qs.q: In which type of operating system are similar jobs collected and executed together without user interaction?
qs.e: Batch OS groups jobs (like payroll) and runs them in batches; time-sharing gives each user a slice of CPU time.

qs.q: An OS that gives each of many users a small slice of CPU time in turn, so all seem to work at once, is called —
qs.e: Time-sharing divides CPU time into slices among users; real-time is about deadlines, batch about grouped jobs.

qs.q: What is the full form of GUI?
qs.e: GUI uses icons, windows and a mouse (Windows); its opposite is CLI, Command Line Interface (MS-DOS).

qs.q: Which of the following is an example of a Command Line Interface (CLI) operating system?
qs.e: In MS-DOS you type commands at a prompt; Windows, macOS and Android are GUI-based.

qs.q: In Windows, where does a file go when it is deleted from the hard disk using the Delete key?
qs.e: Delete moves the file to the Recycle Bin, from where it can be restored; Shift+Delete removes it permanently.

qs.q: Which key combination deletes a selected file in Windows permanently, without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
qs.e: Shift+Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin; Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager.

qs.q: Which pair of file extension and file type is correctly matched?
qs.e: .xlsx is an Excel workbook; .pptx is PowerPoint, .mp3 is audio and .zip is a compressed archive.

qs.q: A file with the extension .exe is a(n) —
qs.e: .exe files run directly in Windows; .xlsx is Excel and .txt is plain text.

qs.q: Software that can be used free for a trial period, after which the user is asked to pay, is called —
qs.e: Shareware is try-before-you-buy; freeware is free but closed source; open source makes the code public.

qs.q: What is the role of a device driver?
o: It lets the operating system communicate with a hardware device
It translates high-level code into machine code
It removes viruses from the computer
It compresses files to save space
qs.e: A device driver (e.g. printer driver) is system software that connects the OS with a specific device.

qs.q: BIOS, stored permanently on a chip on the motherboard, is an example of —
qs.e: Software stored permanently in ROM/flash inside hardware is firmware; BIOS starts the computer during booting.

qs.q: Antivirus, Disk Cleanup and disk defragmenter are examples of —
qs.e: Utilities are system software that maintain the computer; they are not application software.

qs.q: PDF stands for:
qs.e: PDF = Portable Document Format, created by Adobe so a document looks the same on any device.

qs.q: Which shortcut undoes the last action?
qs.e: Ctrl+Z = Undo, Ctrl+Y = Redo, Ctrl+X = Cut, Ctrl+U = Underline.

qs.q: Ctrl+Y is used to —
qs.e: Ctrl+Y redoes (or repeats) an action; Ctrl+Z undoes it.

qs.q: Which shortcut switches between open programs in Windows?
qs.e: Alt+Tab switches windows; Ctrl+Tab switches tabs inside a program such as a browser; Alt+F4 closes the window.

qs.q: Alt+F4 in Windows is used to —
o: Close the active window or program
qs.e: Alt+F4 closes the active window; on the bare desktop it opens the Shut Down dialog.

qs.q: Which shortcut shows the Windows desktop by minimising all open windows (press again to restore)?
qs.e: Win+D = Desktop, Win+E = File Explorer, Win+L = Lock, Win+R = Run.

qs.q: Which shortcut locks a Windows computer?
qs.e: Win+L locks the PC; Ctrl+L in a browser jumps to the address bar and in Word left-aligns text.

qs.q: Win+E opens —
qs.e: Win+E opens File Explorer; Settings is Win+I.

qs.q: Which shortcut opens the Run dialog box in Windows?
qs.e: Win+R opens Run; Ctrl+R in a browser reloads the page and in Word right-aligns text.

qs.q: Which shortcut opens Task Manager directly in Windows?
qs.e: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager straight away; Ctrl+Alt+Delete first shows the security screen.

qs.q: Which function key is used to rename a selected file or folder in File Explorer?
qs.e: F2 renames in Windows (in Excel F2 edits the active cell); F5 refreshes.

qs.q: In a web browser such as Chrome, what does Ctrl+D do?
qs.e: In a browser Ctrl+D bookmarks the page; Ctrl+J opens downloads. Note: in Word Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog and in Excel it fills down.

qs.q: In a web browser, which shortcut reloads the page while ignoring the cached copy (hard reload)?
qs.e: F5 and Ctrl+R do a normal reload; Ctrl+F5 (or Ctrl+Shift+R) forces a fresh download, bypassing the cache.

qs.q: Which browser shortcut reopens the most recently closed tab?
qs.e: Ctrl+Shift+T restores the last closed tab; Ctrl+T opens a new blank tab.

qs.q: In Google Chrome, Ctrl+H opens —
qs.e: Ctrl+H is History in browsers, but Replace in Word and Excel — read which program the question names.

qs.q: In Chrome and Edge, which shortcut opens the Downloads page?
qs.e: Ctrl+J = Downloads, Ctrl+D = bookmark, Ctrl+H = history.

qs.q: In Google Chrome, Ctrl+Shift+N opens —
qs.e: Ctrl+Shift+N opens incognito in Chrome (InPrivate in Edge); Firefox uses Ctrl+Shift+P for a private window.

qs.q: Which of these does NOT move the cursor to the browser's address bar?
qs.e: Ctrl+L, Alt+D and F6 all select the address bar; Ctrl+H opens history.

qs.q: In MS Office programs, F12 opens the —
qs.e: F12 = Save As in Word, Excel and PowerPoint; in a browser F12 opens developer tools.

qs.q: Which shortcut selects all items or all text?
Ctrl+X is the shortcut for —
qs.e: Ctrl+X cuts (moves) the selection to the clipboard; Ctrl+C copies it.

qs.q: Which shortcut opens a new tab in a web browser?
qs.e: Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+N opens a new window and Ctrl+Tab moves to the next tab.

qs.q: In a web browser Ctrl+W —
qs.e: Ctrl+W (or Ctrl+F4) closes the current tab; in Word the same keys close the document.

qs.q: Which key combination opens the context (right-click) menu for the selected item?
qs.e: Shift+F10 works like a right-click; F10 alone activates the menu bar or key tips.

qs.q: Pressing F5 in a web browser —
qs.e: F5 reloads in a browser; it starts the show in PowerPoint and opens Go To in Word and Excel.

qs.q: Which browser shortcut reloads a page and ignores the copy saved in the cache (a hard reload)?
qs.e: F5 reloads; Ctrl+F5 reloads while bypassing the cache. Ctrl+D bookmarks, Ctrl+H opens history, Ctrl+J opens downloads.

qs.q: In a web browser, which shortcut bookmarks the page you are on?
qs.e: Ctrl+D adds a bookmark in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Careful: in MS Word the same Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog, and in Excel it fills down.

qs.q: What is the default file extension of a document saved in MS Word 2007 or later?
qs.e: .docx is the default since Word 2007; .doc was used in Word 97–2003 and .dotx is a template.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts a hyperlink in MS Word?
qs.e: Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink (also in Excel and PowerPoint); Ctrl+H is Replace.

qs.q: Which shortcut closes the current document in MS Word?
qs.e: Ctrl+W (or Ctrl+F4) closes the document window; Ctrl+E centres text and Ctrl+C copies.

qs.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+E is used to —
qs.e: Ctrl+L left, Ctrl+E center, Ctrl+R right, Ctrl+J justify.

qs.q: Which shortcut justifies a paragraph in MS Word (straight left and right edges)?
qs.e: Ctrl+J = Justify; in a browser the same keys open Downloads.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts a page break in MS Word?
qs.e: Ctrl+Enter = page break; Shift+Enter = line break; Ctrl+Shift+Enter = column break.

qs.q: In MS Word, Shift+F3 is used to —
o: Change the case of selected text
qs.e: Shift+F3 cycles lowercase / UPPERCASE / Capitalise Each Word in Word; in Excel it opens Insert Function.

qs.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+] (right square bracket) —
o: Increases the font size by 1 point
Decreases the font size by 1 point
qs.e: Ctrl+] grows text by 1 pt and Ctrl+[ shrinks it by 1 pt.

qs.q: Which key starts the Spelling and Grammar check in MS Word?
qs.e: F7 runs the spelling and grammar check; Shift+F7 opens the Thesaurus.

qs.q: Shift+F7 in MS Word opens the —
qs.e: Thesaurus (synonyms) is Shift+F7; plain F7 is the spelling and grammar check.

qs.q: Mail Merge in MS Word is mainly used to —
o: Create personalised letters for many recipients from one document and a data list
Join two Word documents into one
Send a document by email to one person
qs.e: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source (e.g. an Excel list) to produce many personalised letters, envelopes or labels.

qs.q: Under which tab of MS Word is the Mail Merge feature found?
qs.e: Start Mail Merge, Select Recipients and Finish and Merge are on the Mailings tab.

qs.q: Track Changes in MS Word is found under the —
qs.e: Review holds Spelling, Comments, Track Changes and Accept/Reject.

qs.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+D opens the —
qs.e: Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog in Word; in Excel it fills down and in a browser it bookmarks the page.

qs.q: Which shortcut opens the Replace dialog in MS Word?
qs.e: Ctrl+H = Replace, Ctrl+F = Find (Navigation pane), Ctrl+G = Go To, Ctrl+R = right align.

qs.q: Text that appears at the top of every page of a Word document is called the —
qs.e: The header repeats at the top and the footer at the bottom of every page; both are inserted from the Insert tab.

qs.q: Portrait and Landscape are options of —
qs.e: Orientation (Layout tab) is portrait (tall) or landscape (wide).

qs.q: What is the file extension of a Word template?
What is the default view in MS Word, which shows the page as it will be printed?
qs.e: Print Layout is the default; Draft hides headers and pictures, Web Layout shows the page as a web page.

qs.q: The Format Painter tool in MS Word is used to —
o: Copy formatting from one piece of text to another
qs.e: Format Painter (paintbrush, Home tab) copies formatting only, not the text.

qs.q: The bar at the bottom of the Word window that shows the page number and word count is the —
qs.e: The status bar sits at the bottom; the title bar is at the top and shows the document name.

qs.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+Home moves the cursor to the —
qs.e: Ctrl+Home goes to the start of the document; Home alone goes to the start of the line; Ctrl+End to the end.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts a line break (new line within the same paragraph) in MS Word?
qs.e: Shift+Enter starts a new line in the same paragraph; Ctrl+Enter inserts a page break. In Excel a new line in a cell is Alt+Enter.

qs.q: In MS Word, which shortcut inserts a hyperlink?
qs.e: Ctrl+K opens Insert Hyperlink in Word (and in Excel and PowerPoint). Ctrl+H is Find and Replace, Ctrl+L left-aligns, Ctrl+Y redoes.

qs.q: Which shortcut closes the current document in MS Word, leaving Word open?
qs.e: Ctrl+W (or Ctrl+F4) closes the document. Alt+F4 closes the whole program window; Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager.

qs.q: Which shortcut creates a new blank workbook in MS Excel?
qs.e: Ctrl+N creates a new workbook; Ctrl+W closes it and Ctrl+O opens an existing one.

qs.q: The intersection of a row and a column in a worksheet is called a —
qs.e: A cell is where a row meets a column; a range is a group of cells such as A1:B5.

qs.q: In MS Excel, columns are identified by —
qs.e: Columns use letters (A, B … XFD) and rows use numbers (1 to 1,048,576).

qs.q: How many rows does a worksheet have in Excel 2007 and later versions?
qs.e: Modern Excel has 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns; Excel 2003 had 65,536 rows.

qs.q: What is the last column of a worksheet in modern MS Excel?
qs.e: The 16,384th column is XFD; IV was the last column (256th) in Excel 2003.

qs.q: Every formula in MS Excel must begin with —
qs.e: Formulas start with = ; text starting with # usually signals an error value.

qs.q: Which of the following is an absolute cell reference?
qs.e: $A$1 fixes both column and row; A1 is relative; $A1 and A$1 are mixed.

qs.q: While editing a formula in Excel, which key cycles a reference between relative, absolute and mixed?
qs.e: F4 cycles A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1; F2 edits the cell and F9 recalculates.

qs.q: In the reference A$1, which part stays fixed when the formula is copied?
qs.e: The dollar sign sits before 1, so the row is locked; this is a mixed reference.

qs.q: What is the result of the Excel formula =10+5*2?
qs.e: Multiplication comes before addition: 5*2 = 10, then 10+10 = 20. With brackets, =(10+5)*2 gives 30.

qs.q: Which function counts all non-empty cells in a range, including text?
qs.e: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell; COUNT counts only cells containing numbers.

qs.q: VLOOKUP in Excel searches for a value —
o: vertically, in the first column of a table
horizontally, in the first row of a table
qs.e: V = vertical (looks down the first column); HLOOKUP looks across the first row.

qs.q: The error #DIV/0! appears in Excel when —
o: a number is divided by zero or by an empty cell
qs.e: #DIV/0! = division by zero; #### = narrow column; #NAME? = misspelt name; #REF! = deleted reference.

qs.q: A cell in Excel shows #### (hash signs). What does this usually mean?
o: The column is too narrow to display the value
The formula has a spelling mistake
A number is divided by zero
qs.e: #### is not a formula error — widen the column and the number or date appears.

qs.q: Which Excel error appears when a function name is misspelt, as in =SUMM(A1:A5)?
qs.e: Excel cannot recognise SUMM, so it shows #NAME?; #N/A means a lookup value was not found.

qs.q: Which Excel error results when a formula refers to a cell that has been deleted?
qs.e: #REF! means an invalid reference, usually after deleting the referred rows, columns or cells.

qs.q: Which Excel function returns both the current date and the current time?
qs.e: NOW() gives date and time; TODAY() gives the date only.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts the current date into an Excel cell?
qs.e: Ctrl+; enters today's date and Ctrl+Shift+; the current time; Ctrl+D fills down.

qs.q: Alt+= in MS Excel is the shortcut for —
qs.e: Alt+= inserts =SUM() for the adjacent numbers (AutoSum); Shift+F3 opens Insert Function.

qs.q: Which key lets you edit the contents of the active cell in Excel?
qs.e: F2 edits the active cell (in Windows F2 renames a file); F11 creates a chart sheet.

qs.q: In MS Excel, Ctrl+D is used to —
o: Fill down from the cell above
qs.e: Ctrl+D fills the selection downward (Ctrl+R fills right); in Word Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog.

qs.q: Which Excel feature keeps the header row visible while you scroll down a long sheet?
qs.e: Freeze Panes (View tab) locks rows or columns on screen; Wrap Text only shows long text on several lines.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts a new worksheet in an Excel workbook?
qs.e: Shift+F11 adds a worksheet; F11 alone creates a chart on a new chart sheet.

qs.q: Which file extension is used for a macro-enabled Excel workbook?
qs.e: .xlsm can store macros; .xlsx cannot; .xls is the old 97–2003 format and .xltx is a template.

qs.q: Which shortcut opens a new, blank workbook in MS Excel?
qs.e: Ctrl+N creates a new workbook. Ctrl+O opens an existing one, Ctrl+W closes the workbook, and Shift+F11 inserts a new worksheet in the same workbook.

qs.q: Which key starts a PowerPoint slide show from the first slide?
qs.e: F5 starts from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

qs.q: Shift+F5 in MS PowerPoint —
o: starts the slide show from the current slide
starts the slide show from the first slide
qs.e: Shift+F5 = from current slide; F5 = from first slide; Esc ends the show.

qs.q: Which shortcut inserts a new slide in MS PowerPoint?
qs.e: Ctrl+M adds a slide; Ctrl+N creates a whole new presentation and Ctrl+D duplicates a slide.

qs.q: What is the default file extension of a PowerPoint 2007 or later presentation?
qs.e: .pptx is the default; .ppt is older, .ppsx opens as a show and .potx is a template.

qs.q: The visual effect shown while moving from one slide to the next is called a —
qs.e: Transitions act between slides; animations act on objects within a slide.

qs.q: Which PowerPoint view shows all slides as small thumbnails so they can be rearranged easily?
qs.e: Slide Sorter shows thumbnails for reordering; Notes Page shows the slide with speaker notes.

qs.q: Which PowerPoint feature lets you change the design of all slides at once?
qs.e: Editing the Slide Master changes fonts, colours and layouts on every slide.

qs.q: Which view in PowerPoint is used to see and print the slide together with the speaker's notes?
qs.e: Notes Page shows the slide with its notes below it, as it would print.

qs.q: Which key ends a running PowerPoint slide show?
qs.e: Esc ends the show; Enter or Space moves to the next slide.

qs.q: During a PowerPoint slide show, pressing B —
qs.e: B blacks out the screen and W shows a white screen; press again to return.

qs.q: An effect that makes a picture or bullet fly in within a slide is called —
qs.e: Animation acts on objects inside a slide; transition acts between slides.

qs.q: In MS PowerPoint, Ctrl+D —
o: duplicates the selected slide or object
qs.e: In PowerPoint Ctrl+D duplicates; in Word it opens the Font dialog and in Excel it fills down.

qs.q: MS Access is a —
qs.e: Access is the DBMS of MS Office; Excel is the spreadsheet and Publisher does desktop publishing.

qs.q: In a database table, a field that uniquely identifies each record is called the —
qs.e: A primary key must be unique and cannot be empty (like a roll number); a foreign key links to another table's primary key.

qs.q: Which MS Access object is used to present data in a formatted way for printing?
qs.e: Reports format output for printing; forms are for entering data; queries ask questions; tables store data.

qs.q: Which Access object retrieves records that meet given conditions?
qs.e: A query selects, sorts or calculates data according to criteria.

qs.q: In MS Access, which object provides a user-friendly screen to enter data into a table?
qs.e: Forms are for data entry and viewing; reports are for printed output.

qs.q: What is the default file extension of an MS Access 2007 or later database?
qs.e: .accdb is the modern format; .mdb was used up to Access 2003.

qs.q: In a database table, a single row and a single column are called respectively —
qs.e: Each row is a record (one person or item); each column is a field (one attribute).

qs.q: MS Outlook is mainly used for —
qs.e: Outlook is an email client and personal information manager; it is not a web browser.

qs.q: Which Microsoft application is a digital notebook for free-form notes?
qs.e: OneNote stores notes in notebooks, sections and pages; Publisher is for brochures and newsletters.

qs.q: Google Sheets is the counterpart of which MS Office application?
qs.e: Google Docs = Word, Google Sheets = Excel, Google Slides = PowerPoint.

qs.q: LibreOffice Impress, an open-source program, is equivalent to —
qs.e: LibreOffice Writer = Word, Calc = Excel, Impress = PowerPoint, Base = Access.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Microsoft Office suite?
qs.e: Photoshop is an Adobe image editor; Access, Outlook and OneNote are Office apps.

qs.q: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
qs.e: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the WWW at CERN in 1989. Vint Cerf (with Bob Kahn) designed TCP/IP, the internet's protocol – do not mix the web with the internet.

qs.q: The World Wide Web was developed at which organisation?
qs.e: Berners-Lee worked at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva, when he created the web (1989–91).

qs.q: ARPANET, the forerunner of today's internet, began in which year?
qs.e: ARPANET linked its first computers in 1969; 1989–91 is the World Wide Web, a later service on the internet.

qs.q: Which statement about the internet and the WWW is correct?
o: The WWW is a service that runs on the internet
The internet is a part of the WWW
Both terms mean exactly the same thing
The WWW is older than the internet
qs.e: The internet is the global network; the web (pages linked by hyperlinks) is one service on it, like e-mail is another.

qs.q: In the URL https://www.ssc.gov.in/login, what is 'https'?
qs.e: The part before :// is the protocol (scheme). ssc.gov.in is the domain and /login is the path.

qs.q: What is the main job of DNS?
o: Translating domain names into IP addresses
qs.e: DNS (Domain Name System) works like a phone directory: google.com in, IP address out. Assigning IP addresses is DHCP's job.

qs.q: Which top-level domain is generally used by educational institutions?
qs.e: .edu is for education, .org for organisations, .com for commercial firms and .net originally for network providers.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a web browser?
qs.e: Google is a search engine (Google's browser is Chrome). Firefox, Safari and Edge are browsers.

qs.q: Which was the first widely popular graphical web browser, released in 1993?
qs.e: NCSA Mosaic (1993) made the web popular; Netscape Navigator followed in 1994, Internet Explorer in 1995 and Chrome in 2008.

qs.q: The first or main page of a website is called its:
qs.e: The home page is the starting page of a website. A website is a collection of pages; a web page is a single one.

qs.q: Clickable text or an image that takes you to another web page is called a:
qs.e: Hyperlinks join pages into a web. In HTML they are made with the anchor tag (a).

qs.q: HTML documents are saved with which file extension?
qs.e: .html (or the older 3-letter .htm) is the extension of web pages written in Hyper Text Markup Language.

qs.q: Small text files that a website stores in your browser to remember your login and preferences are called:
qs.e: Cookies remember you; cache stores copies of page files (images, scripts) to load pages faster.

qs.q: Saving a web page's address in a browser so you can open it quickly later is called:
qs.e: A bookmark (Favourite in Edge) stores a link; Ctrl+D adds one in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

qs.q: Sending a file from your computer to a website or server is called:
qs.e: Upload = your device to the internet; download = internet to your device.

qs.q: Watching a video online while it is still arriving, without first saving the whole file, is called:
qs.e: Streaming plays media as data arrives; YouTube and online radio stream content.

qs.q: A private network inside an organisation that uses internet technology and is open only to its staff is a/an:
