qs.e: Intranet = staff only. An extranet lets selected outsiders such as suppliers in. Ethernet is a LAN wiring technology.

qs.q: Which company provides you with a connection to the internet?
qs.e: ISPs such as BSNL, Jio and Airtel connect you to the internet; a registrar only sells domain names.

qs.q: Which top-level domain is the country code for India?
qs.e: .in is India's country-code TLD; government sites use .gov.in. (.id belongs to Indonesia.)

qs.q: Who founded Google in 1998?
qs.e: Page and Brin started Google as a Stanford research project. Jerry Yang and David Filo founded Yahoo.

qs.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
qs.e: Chrome, Firefox and Safari are browsers; Bing (Microsoft) is a search engine.

qs.q: Arrange in the correct order of appearance: (1) Google Chrome (2) Mosaic (3) ARPANET (4) World Wide Web
HTML stands for:
qs.e: HTML is the markup language web pages are written in. It is not a programming language, and its files end in .html or .htm.

qs.q: In e-mail, what does BCC stand for?
qs.e: BCC = Blind Carbon Copy. BCC recipients get the mail but their addresses are hidden from all other recipients.

qs.q: Which e-mail field sends a copy to a person without the other recipients knowing about it?
qs.e: Only BCC hides the recipient. CC addresses are visible to everyone who receives the mail.

qs.q: Who sent the first network e-mail and introduced the @ symbol in addresses?
qs.e: Ray Tomlinson sent it on ARPANET in 1971. Sabeer Bhatia co-founded Hotmail (1996).

qs.q: In the address ravi@gmail.com, what is 'gmail.com'?
o: Domain name of the mail server
qs.e: Before @ is the user name; after @ is the domain where the mailbox is hosted.

qs.q: An e-mail that you have written and saved but not yet sent is stored in:
qs.e: Drafts hold unfinished, unsent mail. The Outbox holds mail that has been sent off but is waiting to leave, e.g. while offline.

qs.q: Messages waiting to be sent, for example while the computer is offline, are kept in the:
qs.e: Outbox = queued, not yet gone. Once delivered to the server, a copy moves to Sent.

qs.q: Unsolicited bulk e-mail is commonly called:
qs.e: Spam (junk) is unwanted bulk mail; mail services filter it into the Spam folder.

qs.q: Which option sends your response to the sender and to everyone in the To and CC fields?
qs.e: Reply goes only to the sender; Reply All adds the other To and CC recipients (never hidden BCC ones); Forward sends to new people.

qs.q: Which e-mail action sends a received message, with its attachments, to a new person?
qs.e: Forward includes the original attachments; Reply and Reply All normally do not send them back.

qs.q: Text such as name, designation and phone number added automatically at the end of every e-mail is called:
qs.e: An e-mail signature is set once in settings and added to each message.

qs.q: Which protocol is used to SEND e-mail?
qs.e: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends; POP3 and IMAP are used to receive mail.

qs.q: What is the maximum size of attachments you can send directly in one Gmail message?
qs.e: Gmail allows 25 MB of attachments; larger files are shared automatically as Google Drive links.

qs.q: Hotmail, one of the first free web-mail services (1996), was co-founded by:
qs.e: Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith founded Hotmail; Microsoft bought it in 1997.

qs.q: NEFT stands for:
qs.e: NEFT is run by RBI and settles transfers in half-hourly batches.

qs.q: RTGS stands for:
qs.e: RTGS settles each transfer individually in real time; it is meant for large amounts (minimum Rs 2 lakh).

qs.q: What is the minimum amount that can be sent through RTGS?
qs.e: RTGS has a Rs 2 lakh minimum and no upper limit. NEFT has no minimum.

qs.q: Which organisation developed and operates UPI?
qs.e: UPI (2016), IMPS, RuPay and BHIM are run by the National Payments Corporation of India. RBI operates NEFT and RTGS.

qs.q: IMPS, the instant 24x7 fund-transfer service, stands for:
qs.e: IMPS = Immediate Payment Service, launched by NPCI in 2010.

qs.q: Which of these transfer systems settles transactions in half-hourly batches rather than one by one?
qs.e: NEFT works in batches; RTGS, IMPS and UPI settle each transfer immediately.

qs.q: To RECEIVE money through UPI, you need to enter:
o: Nothing – no PIN is needed to receive money
qs.e: A UPI PIN is entered only to send money. A request asking for your PIN 'to receive money' is a fraud.

qs.q: Logging in with a password and then entering an OTP sent to your phone is an example of:
qs.e: Two different proofs – something you know (password) and something you have (phone/OTP) – make 2FA.

qs.q: Which of these is a SAFE digital-banking practice?
o: Checking that the bank site starts with https and shows a padlock
Sharing the OTP with a caller from 'the bank'
Writing the ATM PIN on the card
Doing net banking on open public Wi-Fi
qs.e: Banks never ask for PIN, OTP or CVV. Use https sites, keep PINs secret and avoid public Wi-Fi for banking.

qs.q: Which cable is commonly used to connect two computers in a network?
qs.e: An Ethernet (twisted-pair, RJ-45) cable links computers; older direct PC-to-PC links used a crossover Ethernet cable. HDMI and VGA carry video.

qs.q: A network that covers a single building, office or school is a:
qs.e: LAN = Local Area Network. MAN covers a city, WAN a country or the world, PAN a few metres around one person.

qs.q: The internet is the largest example of a:
qs.e: A Wide Area Network spans countries; the internet is the biggest WAN.

qs.q: Connecting your mobile phone to wireless earphones through Bluetooth forms a:
qs.e: A Personal Area Network covers a few metres around one person.

qs.q: Arrange the networks in increasing order of area covered.
qs.e: Personal, Local, Metropolitan, Wide – 'Please Let Me Win'.

qs.q: In which topology are all computers connected to a central hub or switch?
qs.e: Star topology: easy to manage, but if the central device fails the whole network fails.

qs.q: In which topology do all nodes share a single backbone cable?
qs.e: Bus uses one backbone with terminators at both ends; a break in it stops the network.

qs.q: How many cables are needed to connect 6 computers in a full mesh topology?
qs.e: A full mesh needs n(n-1)/2 links: 6 x 5 / 2 = 15.

qs.q: Which topology is the most reliable because there are many alternate paths, but needs the most cabling?
qs.e: In a mesh every node links to every other node, so one failure does not cut anyone off.

qs.q: Which device sends incoming data only to the port of the intended destination?
qs.e: A switch reads MAC addresses and forwards to one port; a hub blindly copies data to all ports.

qs.q: Which device connects different networks and chooses the best path for data packets?
qs.e: Routers work at the Network layer using IP addresses. Your home internet box usually contains a modem and a router together.

qs.q: A modem converts:
o: Digital signals to analog and analog to digital
qs.e: MOdulator-DEModulator: digital computer data is modulated onto analog lines and demodulated back.

qs.q: Which device regenerates a weak signal so it can travel further?
qs.e: A repeater works at the Physical layer; it simply amplifies/regenerates the signal.

qs.q: Which device connects two networks that use DIFFERENT protocols?
qs.e: A gateway acts as a protocol converter between dissimilar networks.

qs.q: Which transmission medium carries data as pulses of light?
qs.e: Optical fibre works on total internal reflection; it gives the highest bandwidth and is immune to electrical interference.

qs.q: Which is the correct order of the OSI layers from bottom to top?
o: Physical, Data link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Physical, Network, Data link, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical
Physical, Data link, Transport, Network, Presentation, Session, Application
qs.e: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away. The third option is the correct order but top to bottom.

qs.q: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
qs.e: OSI (by ISO) has 7 layers; the TCP/IP model has 4.

qs.q: Routing of packets between networks using IP addresses is the job of which OSI layer?
qs.e: Layer 3 (Network) handles logical addressing and routing; routers work here.

qs.q: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
qs.e: IPv6 = 128 bits; IPv4 = 32 bits; a MAC address = 48 bits.

qs.q: An IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.1 is made up of how many bits?
qs.e: Four octets of 8 bits each = 32 bits, giving about 4.3 billion (2^32) addresses.

qs.q: A MAC address, the physical address burnt into a network card, is how long?
qs.e: 48 bits = 6 bytes, written as 12 hexadecimal digits, e.g. 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E.

qs.q: A walkie-talkie, where both sides can talk but only one at a time, is an example of which mode?
qs.e: Simplex is one way (TV broadcast), half duplex is two ways in turn, full duplex is both at once (telephone).

qs.q: The data-carrying capacity of a network channel, measured in bits per second, is called:
qs.e: Bandwidth is expressed in bps, Kbps, Mbps or Gbps.

qs.q: In which network model are all computers equal, each able to share and request resources?
qs.e: Peer-to-peer has no central server. In client-server, a central server provides services to clients.

qs.q: Which of these is normally used to connect two computers in a wired network?
qs.e: An Ethernet cable (twisted pair with RJ-45 plugs) carries network data. HDMI and VGA carry video to a display.

qs.q: What is the full form of HTTP?
qs.e: HTTP = Hyper Text Transfer Protocol, the protocol that carries web pages (port 80). Exams swap Transfer with Transport.

qs.q: What is the full form of HTML?
qs.e: HTML = Hyper Text Markup Language – it marks up web pages with tags; it is not a programming language.

qs.q: In computer security, what is the full form of VIRUS?
qs.e: VIRUS is popularly expanded as Vital Information Resources Under Siege.

qs.q: URL stands for:
qs.e: URL = Uniform Resource Locator – the address of a resource on the web. 'Universal' is the usual trap.

qs.q: CAPTCHA stands for:
o: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
Computer Automated Public Test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
Completely Automated Program to Tell Computers and Humans Apart
Computerised Automatic Public Turing test to Check Human Access
qs.e: CAPTCHA is a Turing-style test that blocks bots from websites.

qs.q: Which protocol is used to transfer files between computers over the internet?
qs.e: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) uses port 21 for control and 20 for data.

qs.q: Which port number does HTTPS use by default?
qs.e: HTTPS uses 443; plain HTTP uses 80; FTP 21; SMTP 25.

qs.q: The default port number for HTTP is:
Which pair of protocol and port is correctly matched?
qs.e: DNS is 53, POP3 is 110 (IMAP is 143), SSH is 22 (Telnet is 23).

qs.q: Which protocol downloads e-mail from the server to your device, usually removing it from the server?
qs.e: POP3 (port 110) downloads; IMAP (port 143) keeps mail on the server, synced across devices.

qs.q: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining a network?
qs.e: DHCP = Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. DNS resolves names; ARP finds a MAC address from an IP address.

qs.q: Which protocol finds the MAC address that belongs to a known IP address?
qs.e: ARP = Address Resolution Protocol: IP address to MAC address.

qs.q: Which statement about TCP and UDP is correct?
o: TCP is connection-oriented; UDP is connectionless
TCP is connectionless; UDP is connection-oriented
UDP guarantees delivery but TCP does not
qs.e: TCP sets up a connection and guarantees ordered delivery; UDP is faster with no guarantee – used for live video and games.

qs.q: Which protocol provides encrypted remote login to another computer?
qs.e: SSH (Secure Shell, port 22) encrypts; Telnet (port 23) sends everything, even passwords, as plain text.

qs.q: VoIP, used for internet voice calls, stands for:
qs.e: VoIP carries voice calls as data packets over IP networks.

qs.q: What does VPN stand for?
qs.e: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network such as the internet.

qs.q: GUI stands for:
qs.e: GUI uses windows, icons and a mouse; the alternative is the CLI (Command Line Interface).

qs.q: The image format JPEG stands for:
qs.e: JPEG is a compressed photo format; GIF = Graphics Interchange Format; PNG = Portable Network Graphics.

qs.q: Which full form is INCORRECT?
qs.e: GIF actually stands for Graphics Interchange Format.

qs.q: CERT-In stands for:
qs.e: CERT-In is India's national agency for responding to cyber-security incidents, under MeitY.

qs.q: IoT stands for:
qs.e: IoT connects everyday objects with sensors to the internet.

qs.q: Which protocol converts a domain name such as india.gov.in into its IP address?
qs.e: DNS (Domain Name System, port 53) is the internet's directory service.

qs.q: HTTP stands for:
qs.e: HTTP is the protocol browsers use to fetch web pages; HTTPS is its secure, encrypted version (port 443 vs 80).

qs.q: Which malware copies itself across a network on its own, without needing to attach to a host file?
qs.e: A worm self-replicates through networks; a virus needs a host file and a user to open it.

qs.q: Malicious software that looks like a useful program but secretly harms the system is a:
qs.e: A Trojan relies on disguise and does not replicate itself – named after the wooden horse of Troy.

qs.q: Malware that encrypts your files and demands payment to unlock them is called:
qs.e: Ransomware holds data hostage; WannaCry (2017) was a famous worldwide attack. Backups are the best defence.

qs.q: Software that secretly records every key you press to steal passwords is a:
qs.e: Keyloggers capture keystrokes; on-screen keyboards on banking sites help defeat them.

qs.q: Software that hides deep inside the system to give an attacker hidden administrator-level control is a:
qs.e: Rootkits conceal themselves and other malware, which makes them hard to detect.

qs.q: A network of infected computers controlled remotely by an attacker is called a:
qs.e: Each infected machine is a bot or zombie; botnets are used for spam and DDoS attacks.

qs.q: An e-mail pretending to be from your bank and asking you to click a link and enter your password is an example of:
qs.e: Phishing uses fake messages to steal credentials. Pharming redirects you to a fake site without your clicking a link.

qs.q: A fraud carried out through phone calls in which the caller pretends to be a bank official is called:
qs.e: Vishing = voice phishing; smishing = SMS phishing.

qs.q: Phishing done through SMS text messages is called:
Redirecting users to a fake website even when they type the correct web address, for example by tampering with DNS, is called:
qs.e: Pharming poisons the path to the site; phishing tricks you into clicking a fake link.

qs.q: Flooding a website with traffic from thousands of infected computers so that genuine users cannot reach it is a:
qs.e: DDoS = Distributed Denial of Service, usually launched from a botnet.

qs.q: Typing malicious database commands into a website's login or search box is called:
qs.e: SQL injection attacks a website's database through its input fields.

qs.q: Trying every possible combination of characters until the correct password is found is a:
qs.e: Long, complex passwords and account lock-outs defeat brute force.

qs.q: Which security system monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic according to set rules?
qs.e: A firewall guards the network gate; antivirus finds and removes malware already on the system.

qs.q: Converting readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable form (ciphertext) is called:
qs.e: Encryption locks data with a key; decryption turns ciphertext back into plaintext.

qs.q: An ethical hacker who tests systems with the owner's permission to find weaknesses is a:
qs.e: White hat = ethical; black hat = criminal; grey hat = breaks in without permission but without malicious intent.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a good password practice?
o: Using your date of birth as the password
Using a long mix of letters, numbers and symbols
Using different passwords for different accounts
qs.e: Personal details such as birth dates are easy to guess.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a type of malware?
qs.e: A firewall is a security tool; spyware, adware and worms are malicious software.

qs.q: The padlock icon and 'https' in a browser's address bar mainly show that:
o: The connection to the site is encrypted
The site is free of all viruses
The site is owned by the government
qs.e: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption; it does not by itself prove a site is honest.

qs.q: A digital signature is used to:
o: Verify the sender and show that the document was not altered
Hide a document from search engines
qs.e: The sender signs with a private key; anyone can verify with the public key. The IT Act 2000 gave digital signatures legal validity.

qs.q: India's main law dealing with cyber crime and electronic records is the:
qs.e: The IT Act 2000 was amended in 2008, adding offences such as cyber terrorism (Section 66F).

qs.q: What is the national helpline number for reporting cyber financial fraud in India?
qs.e: Dial 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in. 1098 is Childline; 112 is the all-emergency number.

qs.q: Which was the first virus for MS-DOS PCs, created in 1986?
qs.e: Brain (1986, Pakistan) was the first PC virus; ILOVEYOU was a 2000 worm and WannaCry 2017 ransomware.

qs.q: In computing, the word VIRUS is expanded as:
qs.e: VIRUS is popularly expanded as Vital Information Resources Under Siege — a program that attaches itself to files and spreads when they run.

qs.q: Who is known as the father of Artificial Intelligence for coining the term 'Artificial Intelligence'?
qs.e: John McCarthy coined the term for the 1956 Dartmouth workshop. Alan Turing laid the theory and proposed the Turing Test (1950).

qs.q: The test that checks whether a machine can show behaviour indistinguishable from a human's was proposed by:
qs.e: The Turing Test was proposed by Alan Turing in 1950.

qs.q: Who is regarded as the first computer programmer?
qs.e: Ada Lovelace wrote an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine; Babbage is the father of the computer.

qs.q: Which statement about AI, machine learning and deep learning is correct?
o: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, which is a subset of AI
AI is a subset of machine learning
Machine learning is a subset of deep learning
qs.e: AI is the widest field; ML learns from data; deep learning is ML with many-layered neural networks.

qs.q: Using Gmail or Google Docs through a web browser is an example of which cloud service model?
qs.e: Software as a Service gives ready-to-use software online. PaaS gives a platform to build apps; IaaS gives virtual hardware.

qs.q: Renting virtual servers, storage and networking from a cloud provider is:
qs.e: Infrastructure as a Service – e.g. Amazon EC2. You manage the software yourself.

qs.q: A cloud used by only one organisation is called a:
qs.e: Public clouds are shared; hybrid mixes public and private.

qs.q: Everyday objects such as smart meters and watches connected to the internet form the:
qs.e: IoT devices have sensors and send data over the internet.

qs.q: A distributed, tamper-resistant digital ledger shared across many computers is called:
qs.e: Blockchain records cannot easily be changed because many copies exist; Bitcoin is built on it.

qs.q: Which technology adds digital objects to your view of the real world, as in Pokemon Go?
qs.e: AR adds to reality; VR replaces it with a fully computer-made world seen through a headset.

qs.q: The basic unit of information in a quantum computer is the:
qs.e: A qubit can be in a superposition of 0 and 1 at the same time.

qs.q: Processing data close to where it is generated instead of in a distant data centre is called:
qs.e: Edge computing reduces delay, e.g. for sensors in self-driving cars.

qs.q: Who created the Python programming language?
qs.e: Python appeared in 1991. Gosling made Java, Ritchie made C, Stroustrup made C++.

qs.q: James Gosling is known as the father of which programming language?
qs.e: Gosling created Java at Sun Microsystems (released 1995). JavaScript is a different language.

qs.q: Who developed the C programming language at Bell Labs?
qs.e: Dennis Ritchie created C (early 1970s) and co-created UNIX with Ken Thompson.

qs.q: The Linux kernel was created in 1991 by:
qs.e: Linux is open source; Torvalds released it while a student in Finland.

qs.q: Which pair of company and founders is correctly matched?
o: Microsoft – Bill Gates and Paul Allen
Apple – Larry Page and Sergey Brin
Google – Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak
qs.e: Microsoft (1975) – Gates and Allen; Apple (1976) – Jobs and Wozniak; Google (1998) – Page and Brin; Facebook (2004) – Mark Zuckerberg.

qs.q: India's first supercomputer, PARAM 8000, was developed by:
qs.e: C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune) built PARAM 8000 in 1991 under Vijay Bhatkar.

qs.q: The Digital India programme was launched in which year?
qs.e: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015; DigiLocker was launched the same year.

qs.q: DigiLocker is mainly used to:
o: Store and share official documents digitally
qs.e: DigiLocker is a government cloud locker for documents such as driving licences and marksheets.

qs.q: Aadhaar numbers are issued by which body?
qs.e: The Unique Identification Authority of India issues the 12-digit Aadhaar number.

qs.q: The first cryptocurrency, launched in 2009, is:
qs.e: Bitcoin was created by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto and runs on a blockchain.

qs.q: Big Data is commonly described by which three Vs?
qs.e: Volume (how much), Velocity (how fast) and Variety (how many kinds of data).

qs.q: Who is known as the father of Artificial Intelligence?
qs.e: John McCarthy coined the term 'artificial intelligence' in 1955–56 (Dartmouth workshop). Babbage is the father of the computer; Turing laid the theory of computing and machine intelligence.

qs.q: How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 100?
How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 200?
How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 1000?
Which is the smallest 3-digit prime number?
Which is the largest 3-digit prime number?
qs.e: 999 = 27 × 37 and 993 = 3 × 331; 991 is prime but smaller than 997.

qs.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
Which of the following is NOT a prime number?
What is the average of all prime numbers between 80 and 100?
x, y, z are distinct primes with x < y < z and x + y + z = 70. Which of the following can be z?
x, y and z are primes with x + y + z = 38. What is the largest possible value of x?
qs.e: 38 is even → one prime is 2; x + y = 36 with y = 5 gives x = 31.

qs.q: What is the sum of all prime numbers from 1 to 20?
0.363636… expressed as a fraction is:
0.2333… expressed as a fraction is:
0.1454545… expressed as a fraction is:
Which of the following fractions gives a terminating decimal?
qs.e: 80 = 2⁴ × 5 has only 2s and 5s; 12, 14 and 30 contain 3 or 7.

qs.q: Which of the following is an irrational number?
qs.e: √12 = 2√3 never ends or repeats; √49 = 7, 0.333… = 1/3 and 22/7 are rational.

qs.q: Which of these is the smallest perfect number?
Which pair is a pair of twin primes?
qs.e: Twin primes differ by 2 and both are prime; 49, 51 and 39 are composite.

qs.q: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
The product of two co-prime numbers is 117. Their LCM is:
qs.e: For co-prime numbers HCF = 1, so LCM = product = 117.

qs.q: Which of the following is the smallest odd composite number?
Find the unit digit of 232 × 235.
Find the unit digit of 628 + 493 + 589.
Find the unit digit of 2383 − 1689.
Find the unit digit of (382)⁵⁷⁵.
Find the unit digit of (187)²⁸² × (529)³²¹ × (343)²³⁶.
Find the unit digit of (789)³¹⁵ + (232)⁶⁴⁴ + (528)²⁵³.
Find the unit digit of (982)⁴⁸¹ − (219)²⁴¹.
Find the unit digit of 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 100!.
Find the unit digit of 7⁹⁵.
Find the unit digit of 3⁶⁵ × 6⁵⁹ × 7⁷¹.
Find the unit digit of 4¹⁹⁹⁷.
Find the unit digit of 9¹⁰⁰⁰.
Find the unit digit of (1739)²⁴³ × (1265)³⁴⁷ × (3418)².
Find the unit digit of 2¹⁰⁰ − 1.
Find the unit digit of 13²⁰⁰³.
Find the unit digit of 8⁴³ + 2⁴³.
Find the last two digits of 31⁷⁸⁶.
qs.e: Tens digit = unit digit of 3 × 786 = 2358 → 8; answer 81.

qs.q: Find the unit digit of 1 × 3 × 5 × 7 × … × 99 (product of odd numbers).
qs.e: An odd product containing 5 always ends in 5.

qs.q: Find the total number of factors of 360.
Find the total number of factors of 480.
Find the number of even factors of 360.
Find the number of odd factors of 360.
N = 56 = 2³ × 7. Find the number of composite factors of N.
Find the number of prime factors of 720 (distinct).
Find the number of composite factors of 720.
How many factors of 720 are perfect squares?
How many factors of 720 are perfect cubes?
How many factors of 720 are divisible by 10?
How many factors of 14400 are divisible by 18 but not by 36?
When 732 is divided by a positive integer x, the remainder is 12. How many values of x are possible?
In how many ways can a pair of co-prime factors of 56 be chosen?
N = 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5. In how many ways can a pair of co-prime factors of N be chosen?
Which of the following numbers has an odd number of factors?
qs.e: Only perfect squares have an odd number of factors: 196 = 14².

qs.q: How many numbers between 1 and 100 have exactly three factors?
qs.e: Exactly 3 factors = square of a prime: 4, 9, 25, 49 → 4.

qs.q: In how many ways can 360 be written as a product of two natural numbers?
qs.e: 24 factors, 360 is not a perfect square → 24/2 = 12.

qs.q: Find the number of factors of 2⁴ × 3⁵ × 5² that are perfect squares.
Find the sum of all factors of 360.
Find the sum of all even factors of 360.
Find the sum of all odd factors of 360.
Find the sum of all even factors of 720.
Find the sum of all odd factors of 720.
qs.e: The power of 2 does not matter: 13 × 6 = 78.

qs.q: Find the sum of all factors of 100.
Find the sum of all factors of 1000.
Find the sum of the reciprocals of all factors of 16.
The sum of the reciprocals of the factors of 28 is:

qs.q: The shape of the pyramid of energy (any ecosystem) is:
o: Upright — it can never be inverted
qs.e: Energy is lost at every step, so it always narrows upward.

qs.q: The shape of the pyramid of numbers in a grassland is:
o: Upright — it can never be inverted
qs.e: Lots of grass, fewer grasshoppers, fewer frogs.

qs.q: The shape of the pyramid of biomass in a sea or pond is:
o: Upright — it can never be inverted
qs.e: A small mass of fast-growing phytoplankton feeds a larger mass of zooplankton and fish.

qs.q: The shape of the pyramid of numbers in a parasitic food chain is:
o: Upright — it can never be inverted

qs.q: The shape of the pyramid of numbers for a tree, its insects and birds is:
o: Upright — it can never be inverted
qs.e: One tree, many insects, fewer birds.
